sanskrit: bhāratānāṃ mahaj janma mahābhāratam ucyate niruktam asya yo veda sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: The great birth of the Bhāratas is called the Mahābhārata; he who knows its etymology is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tribhir varṣaiḥ sadotthāyī kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ mahābhāratam ākhyānaṃ kṛtavān idam uttamam
english: Rising early each day for three years, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana composed this excellent narrative, the Mahābhārata.

sanskrit: dharme cārthe ca kāme ca mokṣe ca bharatarṣabha yad ihāsti tad anyatra yan nehāsti na tat kva cit
english: Whatever here concerns dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, O bull of the Bhāratas — that is found elsewhere too; but what is not here is nowhere else.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājoparicaro nāma dharmanityo mahīpatiḥ babhūva mṛgayāṃ gantuṃ sa kadā cid dhṛtavrataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a king named Rājoparicara, steadfast in dharma, a lord of the earth; though firm in his vows, he once set out for the hunt.

sanskrit: sa cediviṣayaṃ ramyaṃ vasuḥ pauravanandanaḥ indropadeśāj jagrāha grahaṇīyaṃ mahīpatiḥ
english: At Indra's instruction, Vasu, the joy of the Paurava line, that lord of the earth, took possession of the pleasant Cedi kingdom, worthy of acquisition.

sanskrit: tam āśrame nyastaśastraṃ nivasantaṃ taporatim devaḥ sākṣāt svayaṃ vajrī samupāyān mahīpatim
english: To him who had laid aside his weapons and was dwelling in an hermitage delighting in austerity, the god himself — the wielder of the thunderbolt — came in person to that lord of the earth.

sanskrit: indratvam arho rājāyaṃ tapasety anucintya vai taṃ sāntvena nṛpaṃ sākṣāt tapasaḥ saṃnyavartayat
english: Reflecting that this king was worthy of Indra's station through his austerity, Indra gently turned him away from his penance in person.

sanskrit: indra uvāca na saṃkīryeta dharmo 'yaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate taṃ pāhi dharmo hi dhṛtaḥ kṛtsnaṃ dhārayate jagat
english: Indra said: Let not dharma be confounded upon the earth, O lord of the earth — protect it; for dharma, when upheld, sustains the entire world.

sanskrit: lokyaṃ dharmaṃ pālaya tvaṃ nityayuktaḥ samāhitaḥ dharmayuktas tato lokān puṇyān āpsyasi śāśvatān
english: Guard the dharma of the world, ever diligent and composed; yoked to dharma, you will thereby win blessed and eternal worlds.

sanskrit: diviṣṭhasya bhuviṣṭhas tvaṃ sakhā bhūtvā mama priyaḥ ūdhaḥ pṛthivyā yo deśas tam āvasa narādhipa
english: Dwelling on earth while I dwell in heaven, become my friend and dear companion; inhabit that region which is the udder of the earth, O lord of men.

sanskrit: paśavyaś caiva puṇyaś ca susthiro dhanadhānyavān svārakṣyaś caiva saumyaś ca bhogyair bhūmiguṇair yutaḥ
english: That land is rich in cattle, holy, stable, abounding in wealth and grain, easy to defend, pleasant, and endowed with the enjoyable gifts of the earth.

sanskrit: aty anyān eṣa deśo hi dhanaratnādibhir yutaḥ vasupūrṇā ca vasudhā vasa cediṣu cedipa
english: This region surpasses all others, richly furnished with riches and gems; the earth there is full of wealth — dwell among the Cedis, O lord of the Cedis.

sanskrit: dharmaśīlā janapadāḥ susaṃtoṣāś ca sādhavaḥ na ca mithyāpralāpo 'tra svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā
english: The people of that realm are virtuous in character, easily contented, and righteous; there is no false speech even in casual talk, much less otherwise.

sanskrit: na ca pitrā vibhajyante narā guruhite ratāḥ yuñjate dhuri no gāś ca kṛśāḥ saṃdhukṣayanti ca
english: Men devoted to the welfare of their elders do not divide property from their fathers; they do not yoke lean cattle to the plough, and they do not allow the feeble to starve.

sanskrit: sarve varṇāḥ svadharmasthāḥ sadā cediṣu mānada na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu yad bhavet
english: All the social orders always abide in their own dharma in the Cedi realm, O giver of honour; nothing that occurs in the three worlds is unknown to you.

sanskrit: devopabhogyaṃ divyaṃ ca ākāśe sphāṭikaṃ mahat ākāśagaṃ tvāṃ maddattaṃ vimānam upapatsyate
english: A great divine crystal aerial chariot, fit for the enjoyment of the gods, moving through the sky — a flying vehicle given by me — shall attend upon you.

sanskrit: tvam ekaḥ sarvamartyeṣu vimānavaram āsthitaḥ cariṣyasy uparistho vai devo vigrahavān iva
english: You alone among all mortals, mounted on the finest of aerial chariots, shall move on high like an embodied god.

sanskrit: dadāmi te vaijayantīṃ mālām amlānapaṅkajām dhārayiṣyati saṃgrāme yā tvāṃ śastrair avikṣatam
english: I give you the Vaijayantī garland of unfading lotuses, which shall protect you unwounded by weapons in battle.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ caitad eveha bhavitā te narādhipa indramāleti vikhyātaṃ dhanyam apratimaṃ mahat
english: This very mark shall be yours, O lord of men — known as the Indra-garland, auspicious, matchless, and great.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yaṣṭiṃ ca vaiṇavīṃ tasmai dadau vṛtraniṣūdanaḥ iṣṭapradānam uddiśya śiṣṭānāṃ paripālinīm
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The slayer of Vṛtra also gave him a bamboo staff, meant for bestowing desired gifts and protecting the righteous.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ śakrasya pūjārthaṃ bhūmau bhūmipatis tadā praveśaṃ kārayām āsa gate saṃvatsare tadā
english: In honour of that staff of Indra, the lord of the earth had it planted in the ground once a year had passed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti cādyāpi yaṣṭyāḥ kṣitipasattamaiḥ praveśaḥ kriyate rājan yathā tena pravartitaḥ
english: From that time forward, even to this day, O king, the planting of the staff is performed by the best of kings just as he established it.

sanskrit: aparedyus tathā cāsyāḥ kriyate ucchrayo nṛpaiḥ alaṃkṛtāyāḥ piṭakair gandhair mālyaiś ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ mālyadāmaparikṣiptā vidhivat kriyate 'pi ca
english: The next day too the staff is raised by kings, decked with boxes, fragrant unguents, garlands, and ornaments; wreathed with garlands and festoons it is duly honoured according to rule.

sanskrit: bhagavān pūjyate cātra hāsyarūpeṇa śaṃkaraḥ svayam eva gṛhītena vasoḥ prītyā mahātmanaḥ
english: And the blessed Śaṃkara is worshipped here in a comic form, assumed by himself out of affection for the great-souled Vasu.

sanskrit: etāṃ pūjāṃ mahendras tu dṛṣṭvā deva kṛtāṃ śubhām vasunā rājamukhyena prītimān abravīd vibhuḥ
english: Seeing this auspicious worship, done by the gods and by Vasu the foremost of kings, the mighty Mahendra spoke with delight.

sanskrit: ye pūjayiṣyanti narā rājānaś ca mahaṃ mama kārayiṣyanti ca mudā yathā cedipatir nṛpaḥ
english: Those men and kings who shall worship my festival and celebrate it joyfully as the lord of the Cedis has done —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śrīr vijayaś caiva sarāṣṭrāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati tathā sphīto janapado muditaś ca bhaviṣyati
english: — for them, together with their kingdoms, there shall be prosperity and victory, and their realm shall be flourishing and joyful.

sanskrit: evaṃ mahātmanā tena mahendreṇa narādhipa vasuḥ prītyā maghavatā mahārājo 'bhisatkṛtaḥ
english: Thus was the great king Vasu honoured with affection by the great-souled Mahendra, the bounteous one, O lord of men.

sanskrit: utsavaṃ kārayiṣyanti sadā śakrasya ye narāḥ bhūmidānādibhir dānair yathā pūtā bhavanti vai varadānamahāyajñais tathā śakrotsavena te
english: Those men who shall always celebrate Indra's festival — just as they are purified by great gift-bestowing sacrifices with gifts of land and the like, so also are they purified by the Indra-festival.

sanskrit: saṃpūjito maghavatā vasuś cedipatis tadā pālayām āsa dharmeṇa cedisthaḥ pṛthivīm imām indraprītyā bhūmipatiś cakārendramahaṃ vasuḥ
english: Thus duly honoured by the bounteous Indra, Vasu the lord of the Cedis governed the earth from Cedi with righteousness, and that lord of the earth celebrated the Indra-festival out of love for Indra.

sanskrit: putrāś cāsya mahāvīryāḥ pañcāsann amitaujasaḥ nānārājyeṣu ca sutān sa samrāḍ abhyaṣecayat
english: He had five sons of great valour and boundless energy, and that emperor consecrated his sons over various kingdoms.

sanskrit: mahāratho magadharāḍ viśruto yo bṛhadrathaḥ pratyagrahaḥ kuśāmbaś ca yam āhur maṇivāhanam macchillaś ca yaduś caiva rājanyaś cāparājitaḥ
english: The renowned great warrior Bṛhadratha king of Magadha, Pratyagraha, Kuśāmba who is called Maṇivāhana, Macchilla, Yadu, and the warrior Aparājita —

sanskrit: ete tasya sutā rājan rājarṣer bhūritejasaḥ nyaveśayan nāmabhiḥ svais te deśāṃś ca purāṇi ca vāsavāḥ pañca rājānaḥ pṛthagvaṃśāś ca śāśvatāḥ
english: These were the sons of that royal sage of abundant lustre, O king; those five Vāsava kings settled countries and cities with their own names and founded eternal separate dynasties.

sanskrit: vasantam indraprāsāde ākāśe sphāṭike ca tam upatasthur mahātmānaṃ gandharvāpsaraso nṛpam rājoparicarety evaṃ nāma tasyātha viśrutam
english: Dwelling in the crystal aerial palace given by Indra, that great-souled king was attended upon by Gandharvas and Apsarases; thus his name became celebrated as Rājoparicara — the king who roams above.

sanskrit: puropavāhinīṃ tasya nadīṃ śuktimatīṃ giriḥ arautsīc cetanāyuktaḥ kāmāt kolāhalaḥ kila
english: The mountain Kolāhala, endowed with consciousness and overcome by desire, blocked the river Śuktimatī that flowed past his city.

sanskrit: giriṃ kolāhalaṃ taṃ tu padā vasur atāḍayat niścakrāma nadī tena prahāravivareṇa sā
english: Vasu struck that mountain Kolāhala with his foot; the river escaped through the cleft made by that blow.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ nadyām ajanayan mithunaṃ parvataḥ svayam tasmād vimokṣaṇāt prītā nadī rājñe nyavedayat
english: The mountain had begotten a pair in that river; delighted at her release, the river presented them to the king.

sanskrit: yaḥ pumān abhavat tatra taṃ sa rājarṣisattamaḥ vasur vasupradaś cakre senāpatim ariṃdamam cakāra patnīṃ kanyāṃ tu dayitāṃ girikāṃ nṛpaḥ
english: The male child born there — that best of royal sages, Vasu the giver of wealth, made him a subduer-of-foes commander of the army; the king took the beloved girl, named Girikā, as his wife.

sanskrit: vasoḥ patnī tu girikā kāmāt kāle nyavedayat ṛtukālam anuprāptaṃ snātā puṃsavane śuciḥ
english: His wife Girikā, desiring a son, duly informed him that her fertile season had come; she had bathed, performed the puṃsavana rite, and was pure.

sanskrit: tadahaḥ pitaraś cainam ūcur jahi mṛgān iti taṃ rājasattamaṃ prītās tadā matimatāṃ varam
english: On that very day the ancestors spoke to him with affection — to that best of kings, the finest of the wise — saying: "Slay deer for us."

sanskrit: sa pitṝṇāṃ niyogaṃ tam avyatikramya pārthivaḥ cacāra mṛgayāṃ kāmī girikām eva saṃsmaran atīva rūpasaṃpannāṃ sākṣāc chriyam ivāparām
english: Not transgressing that command of the ancestors, the king went forth to hunt, yet, filled with desire, he kept thinking only of Girikā — she who was supremely beautiful, a very second Śrī made manifest.

sanskrit: tasya retaḥ pracaskanda carato rucire vane skannamātraṃ ca tad reto vṛkṣapatreṇa bhūmipaḥ
english: As he roamed in that lovely forest his seed fell; the moment it fell the lord of the earth caught it on a leaf.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha mithyā me na skanded reta ity uta ṛtuś ca tasyāḥ patnyā me na moghaḥ syād iti prabhuḥ
english: He caught it thinking: "My seed must not fall in vain; and the fertile season of my wife must not pass fruitless," so resolved the lord.

sanskrit: saṃcintyaivaṃ tadā rājā vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ amoghatvaṃ ca vijñāya retaso rājasattamaḥ
english: Having deliberated thus and pondered again and again, the best of kings, ascertaining that the seed must not be wasted —

sanskrit: śukraprasthāpane kālaṃ mahiṣyāḥ prasamīkṣya saḥ abhimantryātha tac chukram ārāt tiṣṭhantam āśugam sūkṣmadharmārthatattvajño jñātvā śyenaṃ tato 'bravīt
english: — and reckoning the moment right for conveying the seed to his chief queen, he consecrated that seed with mantras; then, knowing the subtle truth of dharma and purpose, he discerned a swift hawk nearby and addressed it.

sanskrit: matpriyārtham idaṃ saumya śukraṃ mama gṛhaṃ naya girikāyāḥ prayacchāśu tasyā hy ārtavam adya vai
english: "For my sake, dear one, carry this seed swiftly to my home and deliver it to Girikā, for today is her fertile time."

sanskrit: gṛhītvā tat tadā śyenas tūrṇam utpatya vegavān javaṃ paramam āsthāya pradudrāva vihaṃgamaḥ
english: Taking it, the hawk at once soared up swiftly and flew off at the greatest speed through the sky.

sanskrit: tam apaśyad athāyāntaṃ śyenaṃ śyenas tathāparaḥ abhyadravac ca taṃ sadyo dṛṣṭvaivāmiṣaśaṅkayā
english: Another hawk, seeing that hawk coming, immediately rushed at it, suspecting that it carried meat.

sanskrit: tuṇḍayuddham athākāśe tāv ubhau saṃpracakratuḥ yudhyator apatad retas tac cāpi yamunāmbhasi
english: The two then fought beak-to-beak in the sky; as they struggled the seed fell — and fell into the waters of the Yamunā.

sanskrit: tatrādriketi vikhyātā brahmaśāpād varāpsarāḥ mīnabhāvam anuprāptā babhūva yamunācarī
english: There a celebrated celestial nymph named Adrikā, transformed into a fish by a brahmin's curse, was living in the Yamunā.

sanskrit: śyenapādaparibhraṣṭaṃ tad vīryam atha vāsavam jagrāha tarasopetya sādrikā matsyarūpiṇī
english: Adrikā, in the form of a fish, swiftly approached and swallowed that seed which had fallen from the hawk's talons — the seed of Vāsava's descendant.

sanskrit: kadā cid atha matsīṃ tāṃ babandhur matsyajīvinaḥ māse ca daśame prāpte tadā bharatasattama ujjahrur udarāt tasyāḥ strīpumāṃsaṃ ca mānuṣam
english: Some time later, fishermen caught that fish; and when the tenth month had arrived, O best of the Bhāratas, they drew from her belly a human pair — one female, one male.

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ matvā tad rājñas te pratyavedayan kāye matsyā imau rājan saṃbhūtau mānuṣāv iti
english: Thinking it a wonder, they reported to the king: "O king, these two human beings were born from the body of a fish."

sanskrit: tayoḥ pumāṃsaṃ jagrāha rājoparicaras tadā sa matsyo nāma rājāsīd dhārmikaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: Of the two, Rājoparicara took the male; he became the righteous king named Matsya, true to his word.

sanskrit: sāpsarā muktaśāpā ca kṣaṇena samapadyata puroktā yā bhagavatā tiryagyonigatā śubhe mānuṣau janayitvā tvaṃ śāpamokṣam avāpsyasi
english: The Apsarā was freed from her curse in an instant, as the blessed one had previously told her: "O fair one, after entering an animal womb and giving birth to two humans, you shall be released from the curse."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā janayitvā tau viśastā matsyaghātinā saṃtyajya matsyarūpaṃ sā divyaṃ rūpam avāpya ca siddharṣicāraṇapathaṃ jagāmātha varāpsarāḥ
english: Then, after giving birth to those two and being cut open by the fisherman, she abandoned the fish form, regained her divine form, and that excellent Apsarā went on her way along the path of Siddhas, sages, and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: yā kanyā duhitā tasyā matsyā matsyasagandhinī rājñā dattātha dāśāya iyaṃ tava bhavatv iti rūpasattvasamāyuktā sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
english: The daughter, born of that fish and smelling of fish, endowed with beauty and character, adorned with all virtues — the king gave her to a fisherman saying: "Let her be yours."

sanskrit: sā tu satyavatī nāma matsyaghātyabhisaṃśrayāt āsīn matsyasagandhaiva kaṃ cit kālaṃ śucismitā
english: She became known by the name Satyavatī; living with the fisherman-killer, she smelled of fish for some time, though she was sweet-smiled.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣārthaṃ pitur nāvaṃ tāṃ tu vāhayatīṃ jale tīrthayātrāṃ parikrāmann apaśyad vai parāśaraḥ
english: While she was ferrying her father's boat on the water in service to him, Parāśara, wandering on a pilgrimage to sacred fords, saw her.

sanskrit: atīva rūpasaṃpannāṃ siddhānām api kāṅkṣitām dṛṣṭvaiva ca sa tāṃ dhīmāṃś cakame cārudarśanām vidvāṃs tāṃ vāsavīṃ kanyāṃ kāryavān munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Seeing her — supremely beautiful, desired even by the Siddhas, and lovely to behold — that wise and learned bull among sages desired her, that maiden of Vāsava's line, and resolved to act.

sanskrit: sābravīt paśya bhagavan pārāvāre ṛṣīn sthitān āvayor dṛśyator ebhiḥ kathaṃ nu syāt samāgamaḥ
english: She said: "Look, revered sir — on both banks stand sages who can see us both; how could our union take place?"

sanskrit: evaṃ tayokto bhagavān nīhāram asṛjat prabhuḥ yena deśaḥ sa sarvas tu tamobhūta ivābhavat
english: Addressed thus by her, the blessed and mighty sage created a mist by which that entire region became as if enveloped in darkness.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sṛṣṭaṃ tu nīhāraṃ tatas taṃ paramarṣiṇā vismitā cābravīt kanyā vrīḍitā ca manasvinī
english: Seeing the mist conjured by the great sage, the intelligent girl was amazed and spoke, abashed.

sanskrit: viddhi māṃ bhagavan kanyāṃ sadā pitṛvaśānugām tvatsaṃyogāc ca duṣyeta kanyābhāvo mamānagha
english: "Know me, revered sir, as a maiden ever under my father's authority; by union with you my maidenhood would be defiled, O sinless one."

sanskrit: kanyātve dūṣite cāpi kathaṃ śakṣye dvijottama gantuṃ gṛhaṃ gṛhe cāhaṃ dhīman na sthātum utsahe etat saṃcintya bhagavan vidhatsva yad anantaram
english: "And with my maidenhood defiled, O best of twice-born, how shall I be able to go home? Nor can I bring myself to remain at home, O wise one. Considering all this, revered sir, do whatever is best thereafter."

sanskrit: evam uktavatīṃ tāṃ tu prītimān ṛṣisattamaḥ uvāca matpriyaṃ kṛtvā kanyaiva tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: To her who spoke thus, the delighted foremost of sages said: "After granting me my desire, you shall remain a maiden still."

sanskrit: vṛṇīṣva ca varaṃ bhīru yaṃ tvam icchasi bhāmini vṛthā hi na prasādo me bhūtapūrvaḥ śucismite
english: "Choose also a boon, timid one, whatever you desire, O beautiful lady; for my grace has never before been granted in vain, O sweet-smiled one."

sanskrit: evam uktā varaṃ vavre gātrasaugandhyam uttamam sa cāsyai bhagavān prādān manasaḥ kāṅkṣitaṃ prabhuḥ
english: Addressed thus, she chose as her boon a supreme fragrance of the body; and the blessed and mighty sage granted her the desire of her heart.

sanskrit: tato labdhavarā prītā strībhāvaguṇabhūṣitā jagāma saha saṃsargam ṛṣiṇādbhutakarmaṇā
english: Then, having obtained her boon and delighted, adorned with the virtues of womanhood, she united with that sage of wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: tena gandhavatīty eva nāmāsyāḥ prathitaṃ bhuvi tasyās tu yojanād gandham ājighranti narā bhuvi
english: From this her name Gandhavatī became celebrated on earth; people on earth could smell her fragrance from a yojana away.

sanskrit: tato yojanagandheti tasyā nāma pariśrutam parāśaro 'pi bhagavāñ jagāma svaṃ niveśanam
english: Thus she became also widely known by the name Yojanagandha — "she whose fragrance reaches a yojana"; and the blessed Parāśara departed to his own abode.

sanskrit: iti satyavatī hṛṣṭā labdhvā varam anuttamam parāśareṇa saṃyuktā sadyo garbhaṃ suṣāva sā jajñe ca yamunādvīpe pārāśaryaḥ sa vīryavān
english: Thus Satyavatī, overjoyed at obtaining that excellent boon, instantly conceived upon her union with Parāśara, and on an island in the Yamunā she gave birth; the mighty son of Parāśara was born.

sanskrit: sa mātaram upasthāya tapasy eva mano dadhe smṛto 'haṃ darśayiṣyāmi kṛtyeṣv iti ca so 'bravīt
english: He paid his respects to his mother, then set his mind on austerity; he said to her: "When you remember me, I shall appear to you in times of need."

sanskrit: evaṃ dvaipāyano jajñe satyavatyāṃ parāśarāt dvīpe nyastaḥ sa yad bālas tasmād dvaipāyano 'bhavat
english: Thus was Dvaipāyana born to Satyavatī from Parāśara; as that child was set down on an island (dvīpa) he became known as Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: pādāpasāriṇaṃ dharmaṃ vidvān sa tu yuge yuge āyuḥ śaktiṃ ca martyānāṃ yugānugam avekṣya ca
english: Knowing how dharma recedes step by step from age to age, and observing the lifespan and capacity of mortals age by age —

sanskrit: brahmaṇo brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tathānugrahakāmyayā vivyāsa vedān yasmāc ca tasmād vyāsa iti smṛtaḥ
english: — wishing to confer benefit on Brahmā and on the brahmins, he divided the Vedas; and because of that dividing (vyāsa) he is remembered as Vyāsa.

sanskrit: vedān adhyāpayām āsa mahābhāratapañcamān sumantuṃ jaiminiṃ pailaṃ śukaṃ caiva svam ātmajam
english: He taught the Vedas — with the Mahābhārata as the fifth — to Sumanta, Jaimini, Paila, and his own son Śuka.

sanskrit: prabhur variṣṭho varado vaiśaṃpāyanam eva ca saṃhitās taiḥ pṛthaktvena bhāratasya prakāśitāḥ
english: The mighty, greatest, boon-granting Vyāsa also taught Vaiśaṃpāyana; by them the saṃhitās of the Bhārata were published separately.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo gaṅgāyām amitadyutiḥ vasuvīryāt samabhavan mahāvīryo mahāyaśāḥ
english: Likewise Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, of boundless splendour, was born from Gaṅgā through the power of the Vasus — of great valour and great renown.

sanskrit: śūle protaḥ purāṇarṣir acoraś coraśaṅkayā aṇīmāṇḍavya iti vai vikhyātaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ
english: The ancient sage who was impaled on a spike — though no thief — out of suspicion of theft: he became celebrated as Aṇīmāṇḍavya, of very great renown.
